items.section_title: 1.6 · Objective g — Documenting the complete history and physical
items.html: Subjective and objective information. Each is kept in its own appropriate section of the note rather than mixed together.
cites: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 20

src.question: How should subjective and objective information be arranged in a note?
src.key: Each kept in its own appropriate section, not mixed together
src.explanation: Correct — subjective and objective information are each kept in their appropriate sections of the note rather than blended.

items.html: Unperformed examination. History and examination findings may never be made up. If part of the examination was not performed, the note documents why it was not done.
cites: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 20

src.question: What must be done if part of the examination was not performed?
src.key: Document why it was not done — findings may never be invented
src.explanation: Correct — history and examination findings may never be made up; if something was not done, the note documents why.

items.html: Rubor. Rubor means erythema, or redness of the skin; the two terms are used interchangeably.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: Which finding is described by the term rubor?
src.key: Erythema, or redness of the skin
src.explanation: Correct — rubor and erythema are used interchangeably for redness.

items.section_title: 2.7 · Objective d — Abnormal findings: hair and nails
items.html: Terminal versus vellus hair. Terminal hair is coarse and grows on the scalp and in the pubic, axillary and beard areas, while vellus hair is short and fine and covers the body.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: What distinguishes terminal hair from vellus hair?
src.key: Terminal hair is coarse and grows on the scalp and in the pubic
src.explanation: Correct — terminal hair is coarse (scalp, pubic, axillary and beard areas), while vellus hair is short and fine and covers the body.

items.html: Removing dentures. Dentures are removed during the oral examination to look underneath for ulcers and lesions, since a denture hides the mucosa most at risk from chronic irritation.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 67

src.question: Why should dentures be removed during the oral examination?
src.key: To look underneath for ulcers and lesions
src.explanation: A denture hides exactly the mucosa most at risk from chronic irritation.

items.html: Septal hematoma. Injury disrupts the blood vessels and pulls the lining away from the cartilage, so blood collects between the lining and the cartilage.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 57

src.question: How does a septal hematoma form?
src.key: Injured vessels bleed between the lining and the cartilage
src.explanation: Injury disrupts the blood vessels and pulls the lining away from the cartilage, allowing blood to collect between the two.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Weber test. The base of the fork is placed on the top of the head or mid-forehead. The test evaluates unilateral hearing loss by lateralization.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 41

src.question: Where is the fork placed for the WEBER test?
src.key: On the top of the head or mid-forehead
src.explanation: The base of the fork sits on the top of the head or mid-forehead, and the test evaluates unilateral hearing loss by lateralization.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Exostoses. These are benign bony growths in the ear canal. They narrow the canal mechanically, causing conductive hearing loss.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: Which description of exostoses is correct?
src.key: Benign bony growths in the ear canal, causing conductive loss
src.explanation: They narrow the canal mechanically, which is why the loss is conductive.

items.html: Keloid. A keloid is a firm raised scar-tissue lesion, more common in darker-skinned individuals. It is commonest on the shoulders and upper chest but also arises at piercing sites, including the ear.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: A firm raised lesion at an old ear piercing site. Which description fits?
src.key: A keloid — scar tissue, more common in darker-skinned individuals
src.explanation: Keloids are commonest on the shoulders and upper chest but arise at piercing sites, which puts them on the ear.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Viral causes of sensorineural hearing loss. Rubella and cytomegalovirus both damage the inner ear, and both matter most when the exposure was congenital.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: Which viral infections cause SENSORINEURAL hearing loss?
src.key: Rubella and cytomegalovirus
src.explanation: Correct — both damage the inner ear, and both matter most when the exposure was congenital.

items.html: Ophthalmoscope for corneal ulcer. Set at +40 diopters, it in effect fixes a ten times magnifying lens for viewing a corneal ulcer. Fluorescein staining is more sensitive for early ulcers.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 123

src.question: At what setting can an ophthalmoscope be used to look for a corneal ulcer?
src.key: Set at +40 diopters, giving roughly a ten times magnifier
src.explanation: Correct — +40 diopters in effect fixes a 10 times magnifying lens, though fluorescein staining is more sensitive for early ulcers.

items.html: Nodular episcleritis. It can be seen in rheumatoid arthritis and lupus erythematosus.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 47

src.question: Nodular episcleritis is associated with which two systemic diseases?
src.key: Rheumatoid arthritis and lupus erythematosus
src.explanation: Correct — nodular episcleritis can be seen in rheumatoid arthritis and lupus erythematosus.

items.html: Centor rule. It is a clinical prediction rule that uses clinical features to decide how likely a sore throat is to be bacterial, converting findings into a probability and a course of action.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: What is the Centor rule used for?
src.key: Deciding, from clinical features, how likely a sore throat is to be bacterial
src.explanation: It is a clinical prediction rule — it converts findings into a probability and a course of action.

items.html: Eye abbreviations. OD is the right eye, OS the left eye and OU both eyes.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 49

src.question: Which statement correctly defines OD and OU?
src.key: OD is the right eye; OU is both eyes
src.explanation: Correct — OD refers to the right eye, OS to the left eye and OU to both eyes.

items.html: Chemosis. Chemosis is swelling and inflammation of the conjunctiva itself, not of the lids or the globe.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 3

src.question: What is chemosis?
src.key: Swelling and inflammation of the conjunctiva
src.explanation: Correct — chemosis is swelling and inflammation of the conjunctiva itself, not of the lids or the globe.

items.html: Eye pain relieved by topical anesthetic. Relief suggests a surface problem such as a corneal injury, whereas pain that is not relieved may come from a deeper source.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 12

src.question: A patient's eye pain is relieved by a topical anesthetic. What does that suggest?
src.key: Relief suggests a surface problem such as a corneal injury
src.explanation: Correct — a corneal injury feels better with anesthetic, whereas pain that is not relieved may come from a deeper source.

items.html: Hazy cornea in suspected abrasion. If the cornea is hazy in a suspected abrasion, a bacterial infection should be suspected.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 120

src.question: What does a HAZY cornea in a suspected abrasion suggest?
src.key: Bacterial infection should be suspected
src.explanation: Correct — if the cornea is hazy in a suspected abrasion, a bacterial infection should be suspected.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Tuning fork hearing tests setup. Use a 512 hertz fork, the smaller one, in a quiet room. The frequency sits in the speech range and rings long enough to compare two positions.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: Which setup is correct for the tuning fork hearing tests?
src.key: A 512 hertz fork — the smaller one — in a quiet room
src.explanation: The frequency matters because it sits in the speech range and rings long enough to compare two positions.

items.html: Swinging light test. It assesses functional impairment of the optic nerve and the integrity of the visual pathways, and it is indicated for anisocoria.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: Which purpose and indication describe the swinging light test?
src.key: Functional impairment of the optic nerve and the integrity of the visual pathways; indicated for anisocoria
src.explanation: Correct — the swinging light test checks optic nerve function and visual pathway integrity, and its indication is anisocoria.

items.html: Crescent shadow test. Oblique lighting assesses the depth of the anterior chamber angle. A shadow on the medial iris means it is bowed forward into a narrow angle, raising the risk of narrow-angle glaucoma.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: What does the crescent shadow test with oblique lighting assess?
src.key: The depth of the anterior chamber angle
src.explanation: Correct — a shadow on the medial iris means it is bowed forward into a narrow angle, raising the risk of narrow-angle glaucoma.

items.html: Geographic tongue. It is a benign map-like pattern of patches, so recognizing it mainly avoids mistaking it for something that needs investigation.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 71

src.question: What is geographic tongue?
src.key: A benign map-like pattern of patches
src.explanation: Geographic tongue is a benign finding, so recognizing it mainly avoids mistaking it for something that needs investigation.

items.html: Hyperemia. Hyperemia is injection of the superficially visible vessels of the conjunctiva, episclera or sclera.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 3

src.question: What is hyperemia?
src.key: Injection of the superficially visible vessels of the conjunctiva, episclera or sclera
src.explanation: Correct — hyperemia is injection of the superficially visible vessels of the conjunctiva, episclera or sclera.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Conductive causes of hearing loss. These include cerumen, foreign bodies, effusions, exostoses, tumors and tympanic membrane perforation, all of which obstruct or load the external or middle ear.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: Which list contains only CONDUCTIVE causes of hearing loss?
src.key: Cerumen, foreign bodies, effusions, exostoses, tumors and tympanic membrane perforation
src.explanation: Every one of them obstructs or loads the external or middle ear.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Normal Weber result. The sound is heard at the midline, or equally in both ears, with no lateralization to report.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 42

src.question: What is a NORMAL Weber result?
src.key: Midline, or heard equally in both ears
src.explanation: There is no lateralization to report when both sides transmit equally.

items.html: Scalp examination. Separate the hair into sections in order to observe the scalp beneath, including behind the ears and the occiput.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 77

src.question: How should the scalp be examined?
src.key: Separate the hair into sections in order to observe the scalp beneath
src.explanation: Correct — the hair is separated into sections so the scalp can be observed, including behind the ears and the occiput.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Rinne in conductive hearing loss. Bone conduction is equal to or greater than air conduction, because vibrations through bone bypass the impaired external or middle ear to reach the cochlea.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: What is the Rinne result in CONDUCTIVE hearing loss?
src.key: Bone conduction equal to or greater than air conduction
src.explanation: Bone conduction equals or outlasts air conduction, because vibrations through bone bypass the impaired external or middle ear to reach the cochlea.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Rinne test technique. Place the fork on the mastoid until the sound stops, then beside the canal, and ask whether it is still heard.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 43

src.question: How is the RINNE test performed, in order?
src.key: Fork on the mastoid until the sound stops, then beside the canal
src.explanation: Bone conduction comes first, with the fork on the mastoid until the sound stops; the fork then moves close to the canal and the patient is asked if it is still heard.

items.html: Blepharitis. This common eye inflammation is associated with bacterial infection and atopic dermatitis.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: Which two conditions are associated with blepharitis?
src.key: Bacterial infection and atopic dermatitis
src.explanation: Correct — blepharitis is a common eye inflammation associated with bacterial infections and with atopic dermatitis.

items.html: Topical anesthetic in corneal abrasion. It brings immediate relief of an abrasion, but use it for diagnosis, not as a treatment.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 120

src.question: What is the rule about topical anesthetic in corneal abrasion?
src.key: Use it for diagnosis, not as a treatment
src.explanation: Correct — topical anesthetic brings immediate relief of an abrasion, but it is used for diagnosis and not as a treatment.

items.html: Diffusely red eye. Corneal injury, acute iritis and glaucoma can look diffusely red rather than showing ciliary injection; pain, decreased vision, unequal pupils and a hazy cornea (less than perfectly clear) mark these more serious disorders.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 48 (image only)

src.question: Corneal injury, acute iritis and glaucoma can make the eye diffusely red rather than showing ciliary injection. Which clues still point to them?
src.key: Pain, decreased vision, unequal pupils, a hazy cornea
src.explanation: Correct — pain, decreased vision, unequal pupils and a less than perfectly clear cornea mark these more serious disorders.

items.html: Dilated pupils. Document the time of dilation and the agents used; a weak mydriatic reverses in 4 to 6 hours.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 99

src.question: What must be documented when the pupils are dilated?
src.key: The time of dilation and the agents used
src.explanation: Correct — record the time of dilation and the agents used; a weak mydriatic reverses in 4 to 6 hours.

items.html: Xanthelasma. These raised yellowish plaques lie along the nasal portions of one or both eyelids; consider lipid disorders.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 34

src.question: Which description of xanthelasma is accurate?
src.key: Along the NASAL portions of one or both eyelids — consider lipid disorders
src.explanation: Correct — xanthelasma are raised yellowish plaques along the nasal portions of the eyelids that should prompt a look for lipid disorders.

items.html: Subconjunctival hemorrhage and globe rupture. Globe rupture is more likely in trauma, and when the hemorrhage encircles the entire cornea.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: When is globe rupture more likely in a patient with a subconjunctival hemorrhage?
src.key: In trauma, and when the hemorrhage encircles the entire cornea
src.explanation: Correct — globe rupture is more likely after trauma and when the hemorrhage encircles the entire cornea.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Rinne in sensorineural hearing loss. Air conduction is still greater than bone conduction, so the normal pattern prevails, because the inner ear or cochlear nerve fails however the vibrations arrive.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 45

src.question: What is the Rinne result in SENSORINEURAL hearing loss?
src.key: Air conduction still greater than bone conduction
src.explanation: Air conduction stays longer than bone conduction and the normal pattern prevails, because the inner ear or cochlear nerve fails however the vibrations arrive.

items.html: Abnormal pupil findings. A difference in size greater than 1 mm is abnormal, as is a pupil that reacts poorly to direct light.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 71

src.question: Which pupil finding is abnormal?
src.key: A difference in size greater than 1 mm
src.explanation: Correct — a size difference greater than 1 mm is abnormal, as is a pupil that reacts poorly to direct light.

items.html: Pruritus. It is a sensation that causes the desire to scratch and is not itself a diagnosis; treating it as a diagnosis is an error.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: Which statement about pruritus is correct?
src.key: It is a sensation that causes the desire to scratch and is not itself a diagnosis
src.explanation: Correct — treating pruritus as a diagnosis is the error being warned against.

items.html: Kinetic red target test. Move a 5 mm red-topped pin inward from beyond the boundary of each quadrant along a line bisecting the meridians, and ask when the pin first appears red.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 54

src.question: How is the kinetic red target test performed?
src.key: Move a 5 mm red-topped pin inward from beyond the boundary of each quadrant along a line bisecting the meridians, and ask when the pin first appears RED
src.explanation: Correct — a 5 mm red-topped pin moves inward along lines bisecting the meridians, and the endpoint is when it first appears red.

items.html: Pinhole test. It distinguishes a refractive error from other causes: a pinhole passes only light perpendicular to the lens, so a deficit it corrects is refractive; if not, consider cataract or nerve disease.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: What does the pinhole test distinguish?
src.key: A refractive error from other causes
src.explanation: Correct — a pinhole passes only light perpendicular to the lens, so a deficit it corrects is refractive; if not, consider cataract or nerve disease.

items.html: Everting the upper lid in corneal abrasion. A foreign body embedded in the upper tarsal conjunctiva can repeatedly scratch the cornea as the eye opens and closes.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 120

src.question: Why must the upper lid be everted in a corneal abrasion?
src.key: A foreign body embedded in the upper tarsal conjunctiva can repeatedly scratch the cornea as the eye opens and closes
src.explanation: Correct — a foreign body embedded in the upper tarsal conjunctiva can scratch the cornea each time the eye opens and closes.

items.html: Sunken eye from orbital floor fracture. Look for ecchymosis, point tenderness and a palpable step-off around the orbital rim; it is best observed from above the head looking down toward the eyes.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 115

src.question: Which description fits a sunken eye from an orbital floor fracture?
src.key: Ecchymosis, point tenderness and a palpable step-off around the orbital rim — best observed from above the head looking down toward the eyes
src.explanation: Correct — a sunken eye with ecchymosis, point tenderness and a rim step-off suggests a floor fracture; look down from above the head.

items.html: Static finger wiggle test. At arm's length with hands two feet apart beside the ears, wiggling fingers are brought slowly inward until seen, quadrant by quadrant.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 53

src.question: How is the static finger wiggle test performed?
src.key: Wiggling fingers brought slowly inward from beside the ears until seen
src.explanation: Correct — at arm's length, hands two feet apart beside the ears, wiggling fingers come slowly inward until seen, quadrant by quadrant.

items.html: Focused versus comprehensive encounter. In a focused encounter the history and examination are both narrowed to what the presenting problem requires; it is not a shorter version of everything, but a targeted selection.
cites: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 7

src.question: What distinguishes a focused encounter from a comprehensive one?
src.key: The history and examination are both narrowed to what the presenting problem requires
src.explanation: Correct — a focused encounter is not a shorter version of everything, it is a targeted selection.

items.html: Skin assessment. Six characteristics are assessed by inspection, palpation or both: color, moisture, temperature, texture, mobility and turgor, and lesions; color and lesions begin with inspection and the remainder require touch.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: Which characteristics of the skin are assessed by inspection, palpation or both?
src.key: Color, moisture, temperature, texture, mobility and turgor, and lesions
src.explanation: Correct — six characteristics, of which color and lesions begin with inspection and the remainder require touch.

items.html: Dizziness. When a patient says they are dizzy, the history must separate vertigo, presyncope, disequilibrium and psychiatric causes; the word means nothing until the patient explains it.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: A patient says they are “dizzy”. Which four categories must the history separate?
src.key: Vertigo, presyncope, disequilibrium and psychiatric causes
src.explanation: The word means nothing until the patient explains it, and these are the four things it turns out to mean.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Hearing screening and the tuning fork tests
items.html: Frequency pattern of presbycusis. It is a higher frequency loss, so the complaint is about clarity rather than volume, because the high registers carry the consonants.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: What frequency pattern does presbycusis take?
src.key: Higher frequency loss
src.explanation: and it is why the complaint is about clarity rather than volume — the high registers carry the consonants.

items.html: Centor criteria. The four are fever, tonsillar exudates, swollen anterior cervical adenopathy, and ABSENCE of cough; three are things present and one is a thing absent.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 64

src.question: What are the four Centor criteria?
src.key: Fever, tonsillar exudates, swollen anterior cervical adenopathy, and ABSENCE of cough
src.explanation: Three are things present and one is a thing absent, which is the part most often misremembered.

items.html: Microtia. It is an abnormally small auricle, congenitally underdeveloped, and is grouped with atresia among the congenital deformities.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: What is microtia?
src.key: An abnormally small auricle
src.explanation: Microtia is a congenitally underdeveloped, abnormally small auricle, and it is grouped with atresia among the congenital deformities.

items.html: Entropion and ectropion. Both affect the lower lid; entropion is inward folding and ectropion is outward turning.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 3

src.question: Entropion and ectropion both affect which eyelid?
src.key: The lower lid
src.explanation: Correct — entropion is inward folding and ectropion outward turning, and both affect the lower lid.

items.html: Red eye with diffuse redness. Conjunctivitis gives diffuse conjunctival redness maximal peripherally, with vision affected only by mild blurring.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 48 (image only)

src.question: Which cause of red eye shows redness that is DIFFUSE and maximal peripherally, with vision unaffected?
src.key: Conjunctivitis
src.explanation: Correct — conjunctivitis gives diffuse conjunctival redness maximal peripherally, with vision affected only by mild blurring.

items.html: Pupillary constriction in the near reaction. It is mediated by the oculomotor nerve; convergence and accommodation happen alongside it but are not part of it.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 80

src.question: Which nerve mediates the pupillary constriction of the near reaction?
src.key: The oculomotor nerve; accompanied by convergence and accommodation
src.explanation: Correct — the oculomotor nerve mediates the near constriction; convergence and accommodation happen alongside it but are not part of it.

items.html: Eye discharge. Purulent discharge suggests a bacterial infection, while watery or mucoid discharge suggests allergy or a virus.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: Purulent discharge suggests what?
src.key: Bacterial infection
src.explanation: Correct — purulent discharge suggests a bacterial infection, while watery or mucoid discharge suggests allergy or a virus.

items.html: Tympanic membrane mobility. Reduced mobility on insufflation points to an effusion behind the membrane or to a thickened tympanic membrane.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: What does reduced mobility of the tympanic membrane on insufflation indicate?
src.key: Effusion behind the membrane
src.explanation: Reduced mobility on insufflation points to an effusion behind the membrane or to a thickened tympanic membrane.

items.html: Normal fundus and disc. The fundus is yellowish-orange to cream in color, with small disc vessels, a sharp disc margin, and a cup located centrally or slightly temporal with a diameter normally less than half the disc.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 102

src.question: What is the normal appearance of the fundus and disc?
src.key: Yellowish-orange to cream color, small disc vessels, a sharp disc margin, and a cup located centrally or slightly temporal with a diameter normally less than half the disc
src.explanation: Correct — the normal fundus is yellowish orange to cream, with a sharp disc margin and a central cup under half the disc diameter.

items.html: Subconjunctival hemorrhage findings. Pain is absent, vision and pupil are unaffected, there is no discharge, and the cornea is clear.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: Which findings characterize a subconjunctival hemorrhage on examination?
src.key: Pain absent, vision and pupil unaffected, no discharge, cornea clear
src.explanation: Correct — a subconjunctival hemorrhage is painless with normal vision and pupil, no discharge and a clear cornea.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Objective d — Abnormal findings: the skin
items.html: Tinea of the groin. A tinea infection of the groin is tinea cruris; cruris denotes the groin, just as corporis denotes the body and capitis the scalp.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: Which term refers to a tinea infection of the groin?
src.key: Tinea cruris
src.explanation: Correct — cruris denotes the groin, just as corporis denotes the body and capitis the scalp.

items.html: Raised, shiny lesion on the auricle. A raised, shiny, slow-growing lesion with visible telangiectasia should raise suspicion of basal cell carcinoma, which is malignant, unlike the benign lumps.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 22

src.question: A raised, shiny, slow-growing lesion on the auricle with visible telangiectasia. What should be suspected?
src.key: Basal cell carcinoma
src.explanation: Raised, shiny, telangiectatic and slow growing — and malignant, which is what separates it from the benign lumps in the same list.

items.html: Ménière disease. Its vertigo is accompanied by pressure or fullness in the affected ear, with fluctuating tinnitus and a sensorineural loss that recurs and eventually progresses.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 12

src.question: What accompanies the vertigo of Ménière disease, beyond the vertigo itself?
src.key: Pressure or fullness in the affected ear
src.explanation: Ménière disease brings pressure or fullness in the affected ear, with fluctuating tinnitus and a sensorineural loss that recurs and eventually progresses.

items.html: Immediate ophthalmology referral. A chemical burn is emergent and goes to ophthalmology immediately, as do rupture and sudden vision loss.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 124

src.question: Which of these complaints should be referred to ophthalmology IMMEDIATELY?
src.key: Chemical burn
src.explanation: Correct — chemical burns are emergent and go to ophthalmology immediately, as do rupture and sudden vision loss.

items.html: Painless red eye. Subconjunctival hemorrhage is the cause of red eye with absent pain and discharge, an unaffected pupil and vision, and a clear cornea.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 48 (image only)

src.question: Which cause of red eye has no discharge, an unaffected pupil, a clear cornea and no pain?
src.key: Subconjunctival hemorrhage
src.explanation: Correct — subconjunctival hemorrhage has absent pain and discharge, an unaffected pupil and vision, and a clear cornea.

items.html: Psoriasis distribution. Psoriasis characteristically appears in an extensor distribution; the elbows and knees are the classic extensor sites.
cites: PD II Derm - Beck.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: Psoriasis characteristically appears in which distribution?
src.key: Extensor
src.explanation: Correct — the elbows and knees are the classic extensor sites.

items.html: Excessive tearing or dryness. Excessive tearing or dryness comes from obstruction in the lacrimal apparatus or from Sjogren's syndrome.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: Besides Sjogren's syndrome, what causes excessive tearing or dryness?
src.key: Obstruction in the lacrimal apparatus
src.explanation: Correct — excessive tearing or dryness comes from obstruction in the lacrimal apparatus or from Sjogren's syndrome.

items.html: Zygomatic fracture. Findings are flattening of the malar eminence best seen from behind the seated patient looking down, edema and ecchymosis of the temple or infraorbital area, and a palpable step-off on palpating the zygoma.
cites: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 117

src.question: Which findings suggest a zygomatic fracture?
src.key: Flattening of the malar eminence best seen from behind the seated patient looking down, edema and ecchymosis of the temple or infraorbital area, and a palpable step-off on palpating the zygoma
src.explanation: Correct — a zygomatic fracture flattens the malar eminence, seen from behind, with temple or infraorbital swelling and a palpable step-off.

items.html: Hard nodules on the auricle. Hard nodules made of uric acid crystals are tophi, indicating chronic tophaceous gout; they are deposits rather than growths, and on the ear they point to long-standing disease.
cites: PD II ENT 2026.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: Hard nodules on the auricle made of uric acid crystals. Which interpretation is correct?
src.key: Tophi, indicating chronic tophaceous gout
src.explanation: They are deposits rather than growths, and finding them on the ear points to long-standing disease.
